packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/encodeOAuthState.ts:5 — a pure JSON.parse→JSON.stringify round trip that encodes nothing and duplicates decode; returns `undefined`, which zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:27 passes straight into the auth URL
packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:42 — `members` selected but never used; `key: unknown` then `key || {}` bypasses Prisma JSON typing

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — if `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset, a request with no header passes (`undefined !== undefined` is false) → unauthenticated credential writes. Comparison is also non-constant-time

adjudication.rationale: The handler authorizes requests by checking `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. If `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is truly unset at runtime (so `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET === undefined`) and the request omits the header (so `req.headers["calcom-webhook-secret"] === undefined`), the inequality is false and the request is accepted, allowing credential create/update without a secret. The code also uses a plain `!==` string comparison rather than a constant-time comparison, which is a verifiable non-constant-time check in the diff (though the more severe issue is the unset-secret bypass).

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:17 — no HTTP method restriction; GET/PUT/DELETE all execute the credential write path

adjudication.rationale: The new Next.js API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` exports a single `handler(req,res)` and never checks `req.method`. All logic (auth header check, `zod` body parsing, decrypting, and Prisma `credential.update/create`) will run for any HTTP method that reaches the route. This means a `GET`, `PUT`, or `DELETE` request with a JSON body could still execute the credential write path, and a `GET` without a body would likely throw on `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` (causing a 500), both of which are defects stemming from missing method restriction.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 — header name used without `.toLowerCase()` though Node lowercases incoming keys; a mixed-case env value silently 403s everything. Value may also be `string[]`

adjudication.rationale: In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts the secret check indexes `req.headers[...]` using `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` as-is. In Node/Next.js, incoming header names are normalized to lowercase keys on `req.headers`, so if the env var is set to a mixed/upper-case name (e.g., `X-Calcom-Webhook-Secret`), `req.headers[thatValue]` will be `undefined` and the endpoint will always 403. The code even documents it “Should be in lowercase” but does not enforce it. Additionally, `req.headers[...]` has type `string | string[] | undefined`, so a `string[]` value would never equal the secret string, also causing unexpected 403s.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57 — `symmetricDecrypt` + `JSON.parse` unguarded and unvalidated; `|| ""` silently decrypts with an empty key instead of failing closed, and arbitrary JSON lands in `credential.key`

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the decrypted payload is handled as `const keys = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""));` with no try/catch and no schema validation of the decrypted structure before writing it to `credential.key` in Prisma (`update`/`create`). Additionally, the decryption key is defaulted with `|| ""`, so if `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is unset the code still attempts decryption instead of failing closed at the configuration boundary.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — `findFirst` on (userId, appId) with no ordering and non-atomic read-then-update; arbitrary credential overwritten when a user has several for one app, and concurrent deliveries clobber each other

adjudication.rationale:
The new webhook handler looks up an existing credential via `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId: appMetadata.slug } })` with no `orderBy`, then updates that single returned row. If the schema allows multiple credentials per user per app (common for integrations with multiple connected accounts), `findFirst` is nondeterministic and the webhook may overwrite an arbitrary credential.

Additionally, the logic is a non-atomic read-then-write (findFirst → update/else create). Concurrent webhook deliveries can both observe “no credential” and both execute `create`, potentially creating duplicates or causing a unique-constraint error if one exists; concurrent updates can also result in last-write-wins clobbering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — outbound call to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no auth, while the paired inbound webhook requires a secret; asymmetric

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true, the code performs `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId, appSlug }) })` with no authentication material (no secret header, no Authorization, no signature). In the same diff, the new inbound webhook `pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` explicitly requires a shared secret via a configurable header (`CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` / `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME`). This makes the “sync” outbound call unauthenticated and provides no built-in way for the receiving endpoint to verify the caller, which is a concrete security/design gap introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — no `response.ok`/status check, no timeout, no try/catch; an HTML error body flows straight into each app's token parser

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when credential sync is enabled it does `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams(...) })` and immediately returns the `response` without checking `response.ok`/status, without a timeout/AbortSignal, and without wrapping in try/catch. The various callers then proceed to treat the returned value as a successful token response (e.g., Office365 calls `handleErrorsJson(response)` and then zod-parses; GoogleCalendar reads `res?.data`), so a non-2xx response or non-JSON/HTML error body from the sync endpoint would not be caught/handled at the point of fetch and can flow into downstream parsing/usage.
